points.description: Gives the core SOM sequence in pseudocode or ordered steps: arrange/initialise the lattice weights (randomly), then repeatedly sample an input, find the best-matching (winning) neuron by similarity matching, and update the winner and its neighbours using a neighbourhood function. Equivalent wording, or an equivalent ordering that initialises before the training loop, earns the mark. Mentioning only the winner update without the initialisation or the neighbourhood update does not earn it.

Gives the iteration control: reduces the neighbourhood and decays the learning rate (and radius) over time, then checks for ordering/convergence to stop, otherwise loops back to sampling new inputs. Equivalent wording, such as 'repeat until the map converges or a maximum number of iterations is reached', earns the mark. Decay without a stopping or repeat condition does not earn it.

rubric.notes: Two equal 1-mark points split the model answer into its two halves: the core learning steps (initialise, sample, find winner, update winner and neighbours) and the loop control (decay neighbourhood and learning rate, stop on convergence, otherwise continue). Full marks require both halves; a pseudocode answer that omits the decay or stopping/loop condition earns only P1, and an answer with no winner-based neighbourhood update earns neither point. Exact wording is not required.
